facts.text: 상처가 아물고도 계속되는 통증에서 벗어나려는 병사들이 터너스 레인 병원으로 몰려들었다.
facts.quote: Soldiers flocked to the Turner’s Lane Hospital, seeking relief from pain that persisted after their wounds had healed.

facts.text: 역사가들은 전쟁이 끝날 때까지 군의관들이 약 3만 개의 팔다리를 절단했다고 추산한다.
facts.quote: Historians estimate that surgeons had removed about 30,000 limbs by the time the fighting ceased.

facts.text: 미첼은 저먼타운의 보석상 간판에서 조지 데들로라는 이름을 따왔는데, 하반신을 잃은 사람에게 어울린다고 생각해서였다.

facts.text: 화자 데들로는 남북전쟁에서 두 팔과 두 다리를 모두 잃었지만, 사라진 팔다리에서 쥐어짜고 타는 듯한 통증을 겪는다.

facts.text: 데들로는 왼손, 특히 새끼손가락의 극심한 통증이 너무 생생해 잃은 부위가 없다는 것이 믿기 어려웠다고 말한다.
facts.quote: I had begun to suffer the most acute pain in my left hand, especially the little finger; and so perfect was the idea which was thus kept up of the real presence of these missing parts, that I found it hard at times to believe them absent
facts.title: The Civil War Doctor Who Proved Phantom Limb Pain Was Real

facts.text: 친구의 권유로 강신술 모임에 간 데들로 앞에서 영매는 절단된 그의 다리의 유령을 불러낸다. 말 그대로 환상지가 나타나는 장면이다.
facts.quote: A friend convinces him to attend a Spiritualist séance where the medium summons the ghosts of his amputated legs—literal phantom limbs.
facts.title: The Civil War Doctor Who Proved Phantom Limb Pain Was Real

facts.text: 소설 속 '3486, 3487'은 실제 육군 의학박물관 표본 번호였고, 그중 첫째는 애틀랜타 인근에서 부상한 일리노이 연대 사병의 두개골 조각이었다.
facts.quote: The first is a segment of cranium from a private in Company G, 48th Illinois Volunteers, who was wounded near Atlanta on July 21, 1864.

facts.text: 많은 독자가 이 이야기를 실제 회고록으로 착각했고, 배경이 된 육군 신경질환 병원(통칭 '스텀프 병원')으로 기부금이 쏟아졌다.
facts.quote: Many readers mistook it for a real memoir, and donations poured into the U.S. Army Hospital for Injuries and Diseases of the Nervous System (known as “Stump Hospital”), where the story was set.

facts.text: 일부는 데들로를 직접 만나려고 병원을 찾았다가, 그런 사람은 없다는 원장의 말에 실망했다.
facts.quote: Some people visited the hospital hoping to meet Dedlow in person and were disappointed when the superintendent informed them that no such man existed.

facts.text: 일부 강신술사들은 이 이야기를 미첼이 영혼의 존재를 믿는 증거로 삼았다.
facts.quote: Several spiritualists seized on the story as proof that Mitchell believed in spiritualism.

facts.text: 한 논문은 독자들이 이 이야기를 실화로 알고 스텀프 병원에 가상 인물 데들로 앞으로 기부금을 보냈다고 쓴다.
facts.quote: Many people who read this story apparently thought it was a true account and sent donations to Stump Hospital on behalf of the fictional George Dedlow.

facts.text: 남북전쟁 참전 군인들은 미첼이 1871년에 이 용어를 만들기 전부터 환상지 증후군을 잘 알고 있었다.
facts.quote: Civil War veterans, of course, were well aware of phantom limb syndrome before Mitchell coined the term in 1871.

facts.text: 이 글의 작가는 이후 수십 년 동안 익명으로 남았다.
facts.quote: The author of the piece would remain anonymous for decades.

facts.text: 소설의 결말에서 데들로는 죽으면 흩어진 몸의 부분들과 다시 합쳐져 온전해지리라는 희망을 품는다.
facts.quote: This strange encounter gives Dedlow hope that, in death, he’ll become whole again, reunited with his scattered parts.

facts.quote: Since the great French military surgeon Ambroise Pare first described what was to become known as phantom limb sensation, in 1554, the presence of phantom limb has been reported almost universally.

facts.text: 카렐 연구진의 닭 심장 조직 배양은 1912년부터 1946년까지 살아서 분열했고, 닭의 수명을 훨씬 넘겼기에 그 세포는 불멸로 여겨졌다.
facts.quote: From 1912 to 1946, this series of chick heart tissue cultures remained alive and dividing. Since the duration of this culture greatly exceeded the normal chick life span, the cells were deemed immortal.
facts.title: Carrel, Alexis, 1873-1944 | Embryo Project Encyclopedia

facts.text: 20세기 초부터 배양 세포는 영원히 늘어난다는 이론이 지배적이었고, 이는 프랑스 의사 카렐의 닭 심장 연구에 기댄 것이었다.
facts.quote: Since the early 1900s, a predominant theory of cells in culture assumed that cells could multiply and grow forever. This assumption relied on the early twentieth century studies of Alexis Carrel, a physician in France, whose work with chick hearts had convinced many that all cells were immortal.
facts.title: Leonard Hayflick (1928- )

facts.text: 헤이플릭이 결과를 발표하려 하자 친구 조지 게이는 어딘가 오류가 있을 것이라며 말렸고, 세포가 불멸이라는 것은 60년 동안 알려진 사실이라고 맞섰다.
facts.quote: 'You're going to get yourself in a lot of trouble if you publish this because there must be some error going on here.' I said, 'George, you know the experiments that Paul and I did. We can't see any hole in these experiments.' 'I don't care', he said, 'there's something going on, you know, this has been known for 60 years that cells are immortal.'
facts.site: Web of Stories (레너드 헤이플릭 구술 인터뷰)
facts.title: Alexis Carrel's claim that cells are immortal

facts.text: 헤이플릭이 태아 세포주 25개를 키우던 중 일부 배양이 약 50번 분열한 뒤 더는 분열하지 않았다. 세포는 죽지 않고 대사를 계속했다.
facts.quote: While he cultured twenty-five strains of fetal cells, Hayflick noticed that some of the cultures stopped dividing after about 50 cell population doublings. The cells were not dead, as they continued metabolizing, but the cells did not divide.
facts.title: Leonard Hayflick (1928- )

facts.text: 멈춘 배양에서는 세포가 더 커 보이고 분열 중인 세포가 크게 줄었으며, 몇 주가 지나면 분열이 전혀 일어나지 않았다.
facts.quote: And the event was that the cells looked bigger. There were many fewer mitotic figures, that is fewer cells were dividing. And as the weeks went by in those particular cultures, there was no division occurring at all.
facts.site: Web of Stories (레너드 헤이플릭 구술 인터뷰)
facts.title: A surprising observation: older cell cultures stop growing

facts.text: 기록을 보니 분열을 멈춘 것은 인큐베이터의 20개 중 서너 개였고, 모두 열 달쯤 전에 받은 배아에서 나온 가장 오래된 배양이었다.
facts.quote: looking at my records, I then realised an important point and that was that the cultures that had stopped dividing – let's say from three or four of the 20 that were in the incubator – were the oldest ones. That is they were ones that were derived from embryos received about ten months or so roughly prior to this event.
facts.site: Web of Stories (레너드 헤이플릭 구술 인터뷰)
facts.title: A surprising observation: older cell cultures stop growing

facts.text: 같은 기술자, 같은 유리기구, 같은 배지로 키웠는데도 오래된 배양만 멈췄다. 그래서 배양이 오래되었다는 사실 자체가 원인으로 보였다.
facts.quote: The other ones, received a week ago, a month ago, three months ago, were happy and it's important to say that the same technician was culturing these weekly, or semi-weekly and the same pool of glassware obtained from our storage area was used, so... and the same pool of culture media. So it became obvious that there was something about a cell culture that was older producing this effect.
facts.site: Web of Stories (레너드 헤이플릭 구술 인터뷰)
facts.title: A surprising observation: older cell cultures stop growing

facts.text: 수컷 대조 배양은 훨씬 먼저 분열을 멈췄고, 혼합 배양이 멈췄을 때 남아 있던 세포는 모두 암컷이었다.
facts.quote: While the male cell control culture had stopped dividing many weeks before that event occurred. And when we looked at the mixture at the time that it had stopped dividing, all the cells were female.
facts.site: Web of Stories (레너드 헤이플릭 구술 인터뷰)
facts.title: Differences in cell division between male and female cells

facts.text: 이 실험은 '더티 올드 맨 실험'이라 불렸고, 암컷 쪽으로 한 '더티 올드 레이디' 실험도 같은 결과였다.
facts.quote: But this male-female experiment which we at first because of the way I just explained it, we called this experiment the 'dirty old man experiment' for obvious reasons. I should say that we also did the 'dirty old lady' experiment with the same result.
facts.site: Web of Stories (레너드 헤이플릭 구술 인터뷰)
facts.title: The results of the 'dirty old man' experiment

facts.text: 그는 약 50번 분열 뒤 멈추는 것이 바이러스·배지·배양 실패 같은 외부 요인이 아니라 세포 내부의 어떤 메커니즘 때문이라고 꽤 확신하게 되었다.
facts.quote: So we were pretty convinced that this was not an artefact of culture, that the cells' failure to divide after roughly 50 population doublings was due to some kind of internal cellular mechanism and not some external artefact like virus, media composition, culture failure, phases of the moon, anything else that you could invoke.
facts.site: Web of Stories (레너드 헤이플릭 구술 인터뷰)
facts.title: The results of the 'dirty old man' experiment

facts.text: 헤이플릭이 푸에르토리코 대학에서 공개 강연을 마치자 한 여성이 다가와 자신이 카렐 연구실의 옛 기술자였다고 밝혔고, 그는 크게 놀랐다고 회고한다.
facts.quote: I gave a lecture at the University of Puerto Rico, a public lecture after teaching there for a couple of months. After the lecture a woman came up to me and introduced herself as a former technician in Alexis Carrel's laboratory at the time of the events that I had been... that I had mentioned in my lecture and I was stunned.
facts.site: Web of Stories (레너드 헤이플릭 구술 인터뷰)
facts.title: Examining Alexis Carrel's immortal chick cell populations

facts.text: 그 기술자는 배양 조각 가장자리에서 중심 배양과 1mm 이상 떨어진 곳에 세포 '섬'이 따로 생기는 것을 보았고, 세포는 그렇게 이동해 새 집단을 만들지 않는다고 알고 있었다고 한다.
facts.quote: I see at the margin of this clot, a tiny island of cells separated by a millimetre or more from the main culture in the centre of the clot, and I know from my experience in this laboratory that cells do not migrate away from the centre explant and then build another mini explant or mini collection of cells one millimetre away with nothing between.
facts.site: Web of Stories (레너드 헤이플릭 구술 인터뷰)
facts.title: How Alexis Carrel obtained his anomalous results

facts.text: 1929년 증시 폭락 직후라는 때에, 그녀가 거듭 의문을 제기하자 상관은 일자리를 지키려면 그 얘기를 무시하라고 했다고 한다.
facts.quote: By this time it was 1929, stock market crash, people... 20 million people are out of work and after our young lady said for the umpteenth time, 'What's happening in these cultures', her superior said, 'If you want to maintain your job here, you will ignore what you are wanting to discuss.'
facts.site: Web of Stories (레너드 헤이플릭 구술 인터뷰)
facts.title: How Alexis Carrel obtained his anomalous results

facts.text: 헤이플릭의 해석은, 당시 원심분리가 조잡해 배아 추출액에 살아 있는 세포가 남아 있었고, 계대할 때마다 추출액 한 방울과 함께 새 세포를 넣은 셈이었다는 것이다.
facts.quote: The other interpretation is that somehow, the culture was being re-fed with new cells and that was my interpretation because the method of centrifugation in those days was so primitive that the probability of fresh cells still remaining in the fluid portion of the embryo extract was great, and that each time they did a sub-cultivation and put in one drop of embryo extract, they were in fact adding fresh cells.
facts.site: Web of Stories (레너드 헤이플릭 구술 인터뷰)
facts.title: How Alexis Carrel obtained his anomalous results

facts.text: 카렐 연구실에서 일했다는 레이가 배아 추출액을 냉장해 써 보자고 설득해 시험하자 '불멸' 배양이 지쳐 보이며 쇠약해졌고, 카렐은 냉장하면 영양분이 파괴된다고 했다고 헤이플릭은 전한다.
facts.quote: Ray prepared the embryo extract along with the technicians and after outing it in the refrigerator and introducing it into this immortal cell culture, the immortal cell culture began to look weary and tired and failing. And Carrel said, 'You see, I told you that if you put this embryo extract in a refrigerator, the nutrients are destroyed.'
facts.site: Web of Stories (레너드 헤이플릭 구술 인터뷰)
facts.title: Flaws in Alexis Carrel's method of producing 'immortal' cells

facts.text: 이 글이 인용하는 바로는, 1930년 여름 카렐 연구실을 방문한 대학원생 랠프 북스바움에게 한 기술자가 배양을 살리려고 배아 세포를 이따금 넣는다고 말했다.
facts.quote: He cited the experience of Ralph Buchsbaum, a biologist who had visited Carrel’s laboratory as a graduate student in the summer of 1930, to illuminate this point. In Buchsbaum’s short visit to Carrel’s laboratory, one of the technicians told Buchsbaum that they would “add a few embryo cells now and then” to keep the cultures alive.
facts.title: Reassessment of Carrel's Immortal Tissue Culture Experiments

facts.text: 훗날 헤이플릭 한계의 원인은 세포가 복제될 때마다 염색체 끝 DNA 조각인 텔로미어가 짧아지는 것으로 밝혀졌다.
facts.quote: Researchers later found that the cause of the Hayflick Limit is the shortening of telomeres, or portions of DNA at the ends of chromosomes that slowly degrade as cells replicate.
facts.title: Leonard Hayflick (1928- )

facts.text: 1974년 프랭크 맥팔레인 버넷이 이 개념에 헤이플릭의 이름을 붙였고, 2009년 블랙번·쇼스택·그라이더는 관련 유전 구조 연구로 노벨 생리의학상을 받았다.
facts.quote: In his 1974 book Intrinsic Mutagenesis, Frank Macfarlane Burnet named the concept after Hayflick. The concept of the Hayflick Limit helped scientists study the effects of cellular aging on human populations from embryonic development to death, including the discovery of the effects of shortening repetitive sequences of DNA, called telomeres, on the ends of chromosomes. Elizabeth Blackburn, Jack Szostak and Carol Greider received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2009 for their work on genetic structures related to the Hayflick Limit.
facts.title: Carrel, Alexis, 1873-1944 | Embryo Project Encyclopedia

facts.text: 카렐의 배양이 왜 그렇게 오래 갔는지는 이 글이 쓰인 2009년에도 여전히 알려지지 않았다고 적혀 있다.
facts.quote: Although many reassessments have been given, in 2009 when this article is written, what went wrong with Carrel’s immortal tissue cultures is still unknown, and remains a matter for further speculation and discussion.
facts.title: Reassessment of Carrel's Immortal Tissue Culture Experiments

facts.text: 헤이플릭은 카렐의 '불멸' 배양이 '1942년쯤', 약 34년의 이어 가기 끝에 중단되었다고 기억한다.
facts.quote: These cells, this so-called immortal cell culture, was terminated, I believe in 1942 or thereabouts, after something like 34 years of allegedly continuous cultivation.
facts.site: Web of Stories (레너드 헤이플릭 구술 인터뷰)
facts.title: Flaws in Alexis Carrel's method of producing 'immortal' cells

facts.text: '헤이플릭 한계' 항목은 헤이플릭이 이 개념을 1965년 위스타 연구소에서 발전시켰다고 적는다.
facts.quote: Leonard Hayflick developed the concept while at the Wistar Institute in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, in 1965.

facts.text: 헤이플릭은 1961년 논문 「인간 이배체 세포주의 연속 배양」으로 이 배양 결과를 발표했다.
facts.quote: Hayflick published an article in 1961 detailing the results of these cell cultures titled "The serial cultivation of human diploid cell strains."
